text:
Alice: Heads up — thinking we should add a 'simulate' action to deploy-bot that does a full preflight dry-run, emits a release-note draft and a rollback playbook. Low-effort and would cut review time.
Ben: +1. We can reuse the existing preflight checks. Key is idempotent dry-run that doesn't touch pins. Proposed command: `/deploy simulate --target=staging --snapshot=auto`
Chris: Also add `--pin-snapshot` to produce a pin artifact for review without promoting it. That'll let SRE review exact image/hash.
Alice: Example simulated output from the bot (draft):
```
SIMULATE /deploy --target=staging --snapshot=auto
status: PRECHECKS_PASS
estimated_latency_delta: +0.18ms
estimated_cost_delta: +0.6%
suggested_rollback: revert to v2026-02-10 (db-migration-safe)
release_note_draft: "Small perf regressions in vectorizer; opt-in quantization added"
rollback_playbook: /playbooks/rollback-v2026.02.10.md
artifacts: s3://redwood-release-sims/2019001234.json
```
deploy-bot: `/deploy simulate` ran: preflight OK, canary smoke hook pending. Generated artifact s3://redwood-release-sims/2019001234.json (dry-run only).
Ben: We should also add a staged-hooks path so teams can point a repo script to run post-canary validations automatically. Suggest: `--stage-hook=repo/path/to/hook.sh` and a timeout.
Chris: I'll prototype a release-note generator that emits a compact markdown snippet + a minimal rollback checklist. Template fields: component, diff (pins), impact, rollback-commands, post-rollback-validation. Where to keep templates? release-tools repo or ops infra?
Alice: Keep templates in release-tools (same mono-repo as deploy helpers) but have deploy-bot accept `--template=release-tools/templates/minimal` so infra doesn't need R/W to release-tools.
Ben: Also include a change-window param: `/deploy ... --change-window="2026-03-25 03:00-05:00 UTC"` and let the bot attach the window to the release artifact and optionally create a calendar event for oncall.
Chris: Good call. I'll add calendar integration as a toggle: `--calendar=auto|none` and default to none. Prototype tomorrow, @Maya can you take a quick pass at the UX for bot messages? Need the simulated output to be scannable.
Maya: Happy to. I'll mock two compact layouts (summary + expand) later today. :+1:
deploy-bot: Note: simulated artifact written to s3://redwood-release-sims/2019001234.json, dry-run flag set. No pins changed.
Alice: Minor follow-ups: include `--annotate` to attach a tiny human-readable summary to the PR/release ticket, and `--generate-rollout-notes` to auto-fill the release notes checklist.
Ben: I'll add a `release.sh` helper that wraps `/deploy simulate` + `git tag --dry-run` + `./scripts/generate_release_md`. Will PR to release-tools.
Chris: I'll push a draft CLI arg spec and one example hook script tonight. If anyone wants to test, run: `./dev/release-sim --config=examples/small-app.json`
Maya: UX will include an inline 'approve' button that flips a simulated pin into a reviewed artifact (still dry until `--apply`).
Alice: This looks actionable. Plan: Chris prototype CLI + template, Ben wires wrapper script, Maya tackles message UX. We'll reconvene in #eng-releases tomorrow AM for a short demo.
